edges.effect_quant: A meta-analysis of 45 studies with 4681 patients found hydroxyurea reduced albuminuria risk by 58% (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.63) and improved transcranial Doppler velocity (SMD -1.03); in the 1906-patient ESCORT-HU cohort, vaso-occlusive episodes, acute chest syndrome, hospitalizations, and transfusion need all fell within the first year.
edges.population: children and adults with sickle cell disease, especially HbSS-dominant cohorts
edges.mechanism: Hydroxyurea raises fetal hemoglobin, reduces leukocyte-mediated inflammation and adhesion, and lowers hemolysis, thereby decreasing vaso-occlusion and downstream organ injury. Over time, these effects can reduce acute complications while improving laboratory severity markers and some long-term outcomes.
edges.summary: Hydroxyurea is one of the core disease-modifying therapies in sickle cell disease, with consistent evidence for fewer painful and organ-related complications and better hematologic profiles. Its benefit-to-risk profile is strong enough that underuse is now more often the problem than overuse.
edges.caveats: Not every organ endpoint is fully settled, and adherence, dose escalation, and monitoring determine how much benefit patients actually realize. Myelosuppression is real but usually manageable with standard surveillance and dose adjustment.
